headline: High-risk filesystem and clipboard bridge from Open Interpreter to a prompt-leak source can enable prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter ingests local files, clipboard, and stdin/stdout by default, and can execute code with user confirmation; system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak source that may contain attacker-controlled text. Because Open Interpreter has no default isolation and shared state via filesystem, a prompt-injection bridge is plausible even without MCP. The interaction is inferred, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF content from system_prompts_leaks is copied into Open Interpreter via clipboard or files
IF Open Interpreter parses that content as instructions or code
IF no provenance or sandboxing layer is added
mitigations: Disable clipboard/file ingestion for untrusted text
Keep the pair in separate directories
Require manual review before any code block execution
Run Open Interpreter in Docker mode requires-engineering
Add provenance labels to imported text requires-engineering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and has broad network egress, while system_prompts_leaks is a repository of leaked prompts that may be sensitive or proprietary. If Open Interpreter is pointed at shared files, it can exfiltrate contents through configured model providers. The pair creates a realistic leakage path; uncertainty about the exact data class pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in Open Interpreter's working set
IF model-provider calls are enabled for those files
IF the leaked prompt repository is copied into the same workspace
mitigations: Use a dedicated empty workspace
Block network egress for sensitive runs requires-engineering
Do not place secrets in the shared filesystem
Rotate any exposed API keys
Review provider logging settings before use

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its shared_state_with_other_instances is via filesystem. system_prompts_leaks itself is not runnable and exposes no write surface, so direct write-write conflict is limited. Still, if both are used in the same workspace, Open Interpreter can overwrite or commit artifacts produced from the prompt-leak corpus.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory
IF Open Interpreter writes or commits files derived from the prompt corpus
IF no locking or branch isolation is used
mitigations: Use separate git branches or repos
Turn off auto-commit workflows
Add a lock file around shared edits
Stage outputs in a scratch directory
Restrict write access to one agent at a time

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate and execute actions from imported content, while system_prompts_leaks is a source of prompt text that may be treated as authoritative. If the corpus is fed into Open Interpreter and then reused downstream, errors or malicious instructions can cascade into code execution or incorrect artifacts. The pathway is inferred from documented behaviors, not directly observed.
conditions: IF prompt text from system_prompts_leaks is used as input to Open Interpreter
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to auto-run or confirm code blocks quickly
IF downstream automation trusts Open Interpreter output without verification
mitigations: Require a human verification step before execution
Disable auto_run
Separate extraction from execution stages
Add output validation against source text
Log and diff all generated actions

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter touches the entire local machine and model-provider API keys, while system_prompts_leaks is source-available and not runnable. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for the pair, so compliance risk is limited to general handling of local secrets and logs. The other agent is not cited because no distinct compliance regime is stated for it.
conditions: IF regulated data is present on the local machine
IF provider-side logging retains prompts or files
IF the prompt corpus contains confidential material
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace
Review provider retention settings
Redact secrets before ingestion
Use a local-only model provider requires-engineering
Document data handling boundaries
